scope: Independent follow-up on exactly the 18 uncertain associations. No production/data mutation.
decision_rule: Named complete intervention for named indication. Genuine secondary weight/glycemic outcomes establish scope. Safety/pharmacodynamics are not excluded. Differentiate established standard background care from a new experimental combination. Do not broaden specifically named diet categories via synonyms.

rows.evidence_and_reason: The registry design declares SCREENING. Its only primary outcome is the number allocated to each study over 4 weeks. The summary explicitly sends screened participants onward to GZP1/NCT06972459 or GZP2/NCT06972472. This allocation record is not a further independent treatment trial; GZP2 is already attached.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants Allocated to Each Study

rows.evidence_and_reason: The detailed description restricts drug challenge to individuals with diabetes or prediabetes after baseline testing. Participants receive orforglipron for approximately two weeks; the primary drug-response endpoint is the difference in postprandial glucose AUC with versus without drug, plus insulin secretion/sensitivity. This directly tests glycemic pharmacodynamics and must not be excluded merely because the purpose code is OTHER or the study is short.

Randomized tirzepatide versus placebo in overweight/obesity. Although renal sinus fat is primary, percent change in body weight at week 52 is a registered secondary efficacy outcome. Therefore the named intervention is tested for weight effects as well as CKD.
primary_outcomes: Percent Change from Baseline in Renal Sinus Fat Content (MRI)

rows.evidence_and_reason: The registry design declares SCREENING and the sole primary outcome is allocation to ISAs. Its own summary calls this the CWMM screening record. Treatment of interest belongs to LAA2/NCT06603571, which the sponsor identifies as the actual eloralintide/tirzepatide study. Do not count this screening record as an additional tirzepatide treatment trial.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants Allocated to Each ISA

rows.evidence_and_reason: Both official title and stated purpose explicitly investigate bimagrumab and tirzepatide alone or in combination. Part A includes two tirzepatide-alone dose arms with bimagrumab placebo and a double-placebo arm; percent body-weight change is primary. ACTIVE_COMPARATOR labels do not erase this explicit independent treatment evaluation. This differs from GZR18 comparator-only NCT06737042.
primary_outcomes: Percent Change from Baseline in Body Weight

rows.evidence_and_reason: Ixekizumab is pre-existing routine treatment for about 3 months before the decision to initiate tirzepatide. Only tirzepatide is registered as the study intervention, given per label; achievement of at least 10% weight loss is co-primary. This tests new tirzepatide exposure on established PsA standard care, rather than initiating a new experimental two-drug regimen.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving Normalized Functioning Health Assessment Questionnaire - Disability Index (HAQ-DI) ≤0.5 at 12 Months of Therapy
Percentage of Participants Achieving at Least a 10% Weight Loss at 12 Months of Therapy

rows.evidence_and_reason: Tirzepatide versus saline with identical Take Control CBT in both arms. The summary explicitly makes cardiometabolic treatment effects a secondary aim, and body weight and waist circumference are registered outcomes. The claim has no restriction against participants with AUD. This is not incidental overweight alone.

Tirzepatide versus placebo in overweight/obesity plus PCOS. Secondary efficacy outcomes explicitly measure percent body-weight change and proportions achieving 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% loss. The ovarian-function primary outcome does not exclude genuine weight-treatment scope.
primary_outcomes: Improvement of ovarian dysfunction as defined by menstrual irregularity in overweight or obesity-related PCOS
Key Secondary - Improvement of ovarian dysfunction as defined by ovulation frequency in overweight or obesity-related PCOS

rows.evidence_and_reason: The design explicitly compares intensive weight loss achieved with tirzepatide against standard care for obesity-related hypertension. Body weight, body fat and waist:hip ratio are registered secondary outcomes. Tirzepatide is varied and weight loss is the named strategy, not an incidental participant characteristic.

There is a named 73-person tirzepatide exposure cohort and body-weight/BMI secondary outcomes, but the detailed description explicitly pools semaglutide and tirzepatide as a class and says the aim is class-level early hepatic/metabolic index response rather than comparing individual agents. The registry does not establish a separately tested tirzepatide weight effect. Preserve uncertainty instead of treating pooled class exposure as verified single-treatment evidence.

The registered strategy directly varies preoperative tirzepatide for 60 days against ketogenic diet and standard preparation; all subsequently receive standard OAGB surgery. The primary outcome is total weight loss after surgery, and tirzepatide is stopped before surgery. This is an explicitly tested obesity-treatment strategy in a surgical setting; the generic claim has no contrary setting restriction. Registry labels observational although narrative describes randomization; preserve its registered study-kind fact, do not invent a phase.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Total Weight Loss at 1 Year Post-Surgery

rows.evidence_and_reason: The registry itself distinguishes VLCD 600–800 kcal/day from LCD 800–1000 kcal/day and states its objective is LCD. Experimental arm and intervention description explicitly prescribe 800–1000 kcal/day for 8 weeks. A broad calorie-restriction synonym would change the named intervention.
primary_outcomes: Fasting Blood Glucose in millimoles per liter and Fasting Insulin Level in picomole per liter will be combined to report HOMA IR
Weight in kilogram and height in meters will be combined to report BMI in Kg/m^2

rows.evidence_and_reason: The registered primary outcome is diabetes remission. Its linked primary report identifies NCT05754775 and explains that the tested program begins with a VLCD of 800 kcal/day, then increases to 1000/1200 with reintroduction and maintenance. Thus the initially unstated calorie category is now established by the primary report; later refeeding does not negate the initial VLCD intervention.

The registry names low-energy diet plus physical activity. The original protocol prescribes approximately 800 kcal/day, but itself distinguishes prior VLED work under 800; the primary results report specifies 800–820 kcal/day. This is a real diabetes-remission intervention, but its equivalence to the current specifically named VLCD claim should not be assumed from total-diet-replacement synonyms. Resolve the claim scope, not the outcome.

The primary report explicitly identifies NCT04805996 and specifies Modifast 820–890 kcal/day for 12 weeks, describing a low-calorie TDR intervention. Weight and HbA1c are co-primary, so indication is clear; the specifically named very-low-calorie category is not. Do not silently broaden the card to all TDR.

The detailed protocol recruits T2D patients already on stable GLP-1 therapy. Both arms continue the same standard medicines and counseling; only the experimental arm adds Optifast, explicitly registered as VLCD at 800 kcal/day. HbA1c is primary. Diet is the differing study intervention, not background; standard concurrent medicines do not turn it into an experimental multi-drug regimen.

Registry intervention and primary report specify low-energy TDR at approximately 860 kcal/day. Its safety aim in a diabetes-remission program is legitimate and not a reason to exclude. The unresolved point is whether this calorie category belongs to the current specifically named VLCD card; do not infer it from similar weight-management intent.
primary_outcomes: Global score of disordered eating psychopathology

rows.evidence_and_reason: The registry describes a hypocaloric TDR regimen of approximately 800–850 kcal/day with food reintroduction. Diabetes remission is primary. The record does not call its tested regimen VLCD; current card scope needs resolution before treating this dose/category as synonymous. Do not reject merely for including routine lifestyle support.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients achieving diabetes remission

remaining_limits: Five holds are not verified matches and should not be silently published as such. Four need a diet-identity/scope decision; one needs a rule/evidence decision on pooled class-level observational research. This does not re-audit every card or every source claim.
